claims.text: The starting composite contains 67.5 wt.% CoCrFeNiMo0.2 matrix powder, 12.5 wt.% Ni-coated MoS2, 15 wt.% Ag, and 5 wt.% Cr2O3.
The Mo0.2 matrix is primarily an FCC solid solution with minimal detectable σ phase.
Increasing Mo from x = 0.2 to x = 1 induces greater distortion of the FCC lattice.
Increasing Mo from x = 0.2 to x = 1 increases the volume fraction of a hard, Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase.
At low temperatures, the Mo1 modification supports the formation or retention of Ni/MoS2-based lubricating films.
At 600–800 °C, the Mo1 modification facilitates oxidation and tribochemical reactions that form a continuous, dense silver-molybdate/oxide glaze.
The high-temperature glaze forms at matrix boundaries associated with Ag, Ni/MoS2, and Cr2O3.
Mo-induced solid-solution strengthening contributes to reduced low-temperature friction.
Ni/MoS2 and soft Ag provide low-temperature lubricating action that reduces friction.
The dense high-temperature oxide/molybdate glaze reduces interfacial shear and material removal.
The σ phase increases hardness and resistance to plastic deformation.
Relative to the Mo0.2 composite, the Mo1 composite will have higher hardness.
Relative to the Mo0.2 composite, the Mo1 composite will have lower wear rates across the tested temperature range.
Relative to the Mo0.2 composite, the Mo1 composite will maintain a more stable low coefficient of friction from room temperature through 800 °C.
Glaze formation at 800 °C will notably reduce both friction and wear.
The friction benefit at 200–400 °C may be smaller than the benefit at higher temperatures.
The baseline Mo0.2 composite has a Vickers hardness of 432 HV and a yield strength of 445 MPa.
The baseline Mo0.2 composite has friction coefficients of approximately 0.66 at room temperature, 0.75 at 200 °C, and 0.21 at 800 °C.
The baseline Mo0.2 composite has wear rates of 13.1 × 10^-6 mm3/N·m at room temperature, 98.1 × 10^-6 mm3/N·m at 400 °C, and 6.6 × 10^-6 mm3/N·m at 800 °C.
The predicted performance may not extend to substantially different loads, environments, or counterface materials.
